confidence_notes: I ran five web searches: one for the RBA rate and four for Punta Cana food and drink prices. Sources were mostly crowd-sourced or undated aggregates (MyLifeElsewhere, Travel Tables updated July 2023, travel guides), and they disagree. Beer ran from about $2.30 at a corner shop to about $6 at a beach bar or resort bar. Cappuccino was about $1.67-$2.36 in the aggregates. An inexpensive meal was about $7-8, and a mid-range meal for two was about $50-62. I set the anchors above the local-average figures because most visitors eat in the tourist zone. I found no Punta Cana cocktail or glass-of-wine prices, so cocktail is about 2.3x beer and wine about 1.9x beer, informed by one guide's roughly $12 cocktail figure. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge and were not searched or checked against listings. The hostel anchors are the least certain because Punta Cana has few registered hostels. The 3-star figure assumes room-only rates, since many local 3-star hotels sell all-inclusive packages. Prices swing widely between local spots and resort-area venues.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on Dominican Republic tourist-area pricing, which is above the national average. Broadly comparable to other Caribbean and Mexican resort areas such as Playa del Carmen, with local-style eateries cheaper than resort-zone venues.
